newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products - Gasoline firm on Nigeria interest.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products - Gasoline firm on Nigeria interest.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products prices ended mixed on Friday, traders said.

Gasoline was firmer. Anticipated buying from Nigeria was still supportive for low octane product while Italian buying and more attractive arbitrage to the U.S. with cheaper freight costs continued to underpin prices for tighter high octane oil.

Traders said the trans-Atlantic arbitrage window appeared nearly ready to reopen. Some saw a gap of around $3 a tonne but others said an increase in New York gasoline prices of about 0.50 cent a gallon or decrease in prices in Europe of the same level could reopen trans-Atlantic options.
Eurograde cargoes steady around $191 a tonne cif Med.
Naphtha markets were illiquid with trading dulled by an industry conference but firmer crude held prices steady around $171 a tonne cif Med.
Gas oil was steady in a typically quiet Friday market.
EN590 premiums were talked in the quotes fob hi +$1.50/+$3.0 range in what most regarded as a fairly balanced market.
"There's not that much material about but at the same there's not that much demand out there," one traders said.
Premiums for 0.2 percent material were talked at around quotes fob hi -$1.0/flat.
High sulphur was quiet with a trading house said still offering a large cargo out of Bilbao.
Traders said buying interest was low for the lower quality material, adding that the cargo may move trans-Atlantic soon, leaving prompt avails in the Med a little on the low side.
One percent cracked was also quiet, with a Spanish refiner said still offering some material.
Low sulphur straight-run fetched good numbers, with two Libyan pieces reported sold to an Italian refiner at high cif Med plus $6 and one Russian sold at $10 over high cif.
